MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron fires on the final, phrase-completing token of a fixed expression or clause — the word that closes the construction (e.g. "one" in "all but one", "c" in "cmd + c", "Now" in "Update Now", "floor" in "fall on the floor", "would" in "yes, I would") — and is strongly suppressed on clause-continuing connectives like "and" and instruction-initial verbs ("Shape", "scheduled").

Rather than a lexical trigger, this neuron fires on ordinary mid-sentence continuation tokens (word-completing suffixes, function words, adverbs) inside formal academic/historical/literary prose — e.g. "-ian" in "Newtonian", " know", " apparently", " of", " more" — and is strongly suppressed by the analogous predictable tokens in commercial/listing or boilerplate web text (car-feature lists, store names, alumni sign-ups).
